children: Industrial production in France stumbled in July, adding to downside risk for overall eurozone manufacturing after the decline in German reported earlier this week, Pantheon Macroeconomics' Claus Vistesen. Output dropped 0.4% on month at the start of the third quarter, below consensus of a small increase, after a downwardly revised 0.1% decline in June. The decline was broad-based, but propelled by transport equipment. Production there dropped 2.8%, extending June's decline, "indicating that the otherwise solid upturn in aerospace output--which boosted industry in the second quarter--is now coming off the boil," Vistesen says. The better news is that business surveys still look decent, after a rebound in August's manufacturing output PMI and with the Insee production index holding up, he says. (edward.frankl@wsj.com)
